conviction_note: Slight long lean (p_up 55) on abs_move 10.0, which gives +1.0 scaled. The reasons for the lean: three straight quarters beat the top of the revenue guide by $8-13m and the stock rose each time; the stock fell 23.9% in 20 days against -14.0% for IGV, so the bar has come down; and the 8 Sep conference repeated that the FY27 guide already allows for supply problems and more future start dates. Pulling it back toward 50: the same quarter last year ended in a -17.75% guide cut on future start dates, the chief commercial officer left in the quarter's last month, the EPS bar is disputed (whisper $0.71 against $0.53-0.60), and the skew mildly favours downside. impact_sum (+2.2) and the scaled number (+1.0) agree in sign. The sum is larger because the small positives are sized on their own.

Two agreeing estimates plus a company guide, so the revenue bar is sourced. The EPS bar is disputed: $0.60 (EW, possibly the Q4 actual mislabelled), $0.53 (Benzinga), $0.54 (Benzinga via search), whisper $0.71. EPS-based findings are capped small.

expectations.real_bar: For the stock to rise, revenue has to beat the top of the guide again (about $770m or more against $761.8m consensus), ARR growth has to hold near 16%, the quarter must show no repeat of last year's late-quarter future-start-date slippage, the FY27 range of $3.18-3.23bn has to be held or raised, and the Q2 guide has to sit around or above the roughly $820m street.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Q2 FY27 revenue $820.0m (Benzinga, undated, as surfaced in search: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NTNX/earnings-forecasts)
next_guide.street_full_year: FY27 revenue $3.22bn on average (range $3.2-3.3bn) and EPS $2.33, updated 2026-11-19 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ntnx/forecast/)
next_guide.company_current_guide: FY27 revenue $3.18-3.23bn, non-GAAP op margin 24-25%, FCF $850-950m (guided 2026-08-26). Q1 FY27 $755-765m. No Q2 guide yet.
next_guide.basis: The street's $3.22bn already sits above the $3.205bn guide midpoint. The guide was built with conservatism for supply, future start dates, a slower renewals cohort and the restructuring (William Blair via Blocks & Files; reiterated at Communacopia on 8 Sep). Management said in August it sees 'no near-term letup' in hardware prices, and TrendForce has server DRAM undersupplied through 4Q26. So the base case is the FY range held, or raised only by the Q1 beat, landing about at the street. A cut like last year's Q1 is the tail risk.

findings.finding: NTNX fell 23.85% in the 20 sessions into the print (72.74 to 55.39) against -14.0% for IGV over the same days, and 2.0% in the last 5 sessions against IGV +0.4%. It now trades 27% below its 2026-10-12 high of $75.98, so about 10 points of underperformance against software has lowered the bar into a print where the last three reactions were +4.0%, +4.8% and +6.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline: the last three prints (after beats above the top of the guide) went +3.98, +4.81 and +6.81. In Nov 2025 the stock went into Q1 FY26 without a drawdown, then fell 17.75% on a guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The price path is priced by definition. The claim is about the reaction function: after a 10-pt relative de-rating with no company news (no 8-K in November, no target cuts found), an in-line-to-beat print should not find holders who still need to sell. If the market had expected a clean beat, the stock would not sit below the lowest analyst target ($63).
findings.independence: IGV path from a separate series: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/IGV?range=2mo&interval=1d. Target dispersion: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/ntnx/forecast/

findings.finding: Nutanix has beaten the top of its own revenue guide in each of the last three quarters: Q2 FY26 $722.8m against $705-715m, Q3 FY26 $703m against $680-690m, Q4 FY26 $757.1m against $725-745m, each by $8-13m. The same pattern on a $755-765m Q1 guide implies about $773-778m, 1.5-2% above the $761.8m consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The three top-of-guide beats paid +3.98%, +4.81% and +6.81%. The one revenue miss (Q1 FY26, $670.6m against $676.6m) fell 17.75%, but it came with a guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: A beat is the base case, and consensus at $761.8m already sits above the guide midpoint, so part of this is priced. What is not priced is the size: consensus is only $1.8m above the midpoint, while the company's recent habit is $10m or more above the top. A market that expected that would carry consensus nearer $770m.

findings.finding: At Goldman Sachs Communacopia on 2026-09-08, five weeks into Q1, management repeated the FY27 assumptions (continued supply headwinds, a higher share of future start dates, slower renewal-cohort growth), said external storage bookings 'rose sharply', and said it was adding specialist sellers. There was no warning and no pre-release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No pre-release or intra-quarter guide change found for this name. In Q1 FY26 the slippage was disclosed only at the print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, so it is largely priced. It is filed because it says the conservatism was built in before the quarter and confirmed partway through. The page's summary is AI-generated and the transcript was not read, so this is sized small.
findings.independence: The August guide's conservatism factors (William Blair via Blocks & Files): https://www.blocksandfiles.com/hci/2026/08/27/nutanix-grows-despite-hardware-price-rises/5292962

findings.finding: President and Chief Commercial Officer Tarkan Maner stepped down in early October 2026 (8-K filed 2026-10-07), in the last month of the Aug-Oct quarter, and CEO Ramaswami took over sales, marketing and customer experience. This raises execution risk on late-quarter bookings, the exact line that slipped in Q1 FY26.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock was flat at 73.41 on 10-05 and 10-06 on 3.4m and 4.3m shares, then made a 52-week high on 10-12, so the market looked through it at the time. Q1 FY26 late-quarter bookings with out-of-quarter start dates led to a 17.75% fall.
findings.why_not_priced: It was public seven weeks ago and the price ignored it then. The effect on October close rates becomes visible only at the print, and nothing quantifies it. This is an inference, not a number.
findings.independence: Simply Wall St on the CEO taking over sales, 2026-10-07: https://www.webull.com/news/15704585770320896 (the same event).

findings.finding: TrendForce (2026-09-30, with an Oct-30 bulletin) has server DRAM undersupplied in 4Q26, conventional DRAM contract prices up 10-15% QoQ, and server DRAM prices still rising in October. That means the hardware-cost and lead-time headwind on Nutanix's customers did not ease during Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Supply-driven timing caused the Q1 FY26 guide cut (-17.75%). Since then guides that embed supply constraints have been beaten.
findings.why_not_priced: It lands inside the guide: management said in August it sees 'no near-term letup' and built continued price increases into FY27. Transmission from macro to company is unconfirmed, so it is sized near 0.

findings.finding: Lenovo, a Nutanix OEM partner, reported on 2026-11-19 for its July-September quarter: ISG revenue $11.3bn (+178% YoY), first place in global x86 server shipments at 16% share (+6 pts), and Enterprise & SMB revenue +200%. Enterprise servers were shipping in volume through two of Nutanix's three Q1 months despite the component squeeze.
findings.link: Lenovo sells Nutanix software on ThinkAgile HX servers and is named among the 'expanded partnerships' in Nutanix's external storage push (TechTarget). Nutanix does not disclose Lenovo's share of revenue. Quarters overlap for August and September.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No reaction history for Nutanix on OEM prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out after Nutanix last spoke, and NTNX fell 5.3% the next session (11-20) with IGV, so no read-through showed in the price. Much of Lenovo's growth is AI/GPU and CSP, and it also cites rising component costs, so this is a proxy and sized small.

findings.finding: Cisco reported its Aug-Oct quarter (the same quarter as Nutanix Q1) on 2026-11-12: revenue $18.5bn (+24%), product +32%, and a raised FY27 guide to $74.8-75.8bn from $72.2-73.4bn. Enterprise infrastructure spend held up through October.
findings.link: Cisco resells Nutanix HCI on UCS (Cisco Compute Hyperconverged with Nutanix), an expanded partnership per TechTarget. The share of Nutanix revenue is not stated. Cisco's growth is led by networking (+43%) and hyperscaler AI, not compute.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public, and NTNX did not respond (60.87 on 11-12, then down). The link to Nutanix's own line is indirect, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: The street's FY27 revenue ($3.22bn, range $3.2-3.3bn, 2026-11-19) already sits $15m above the company's $3.205bn midpoint. The street's Q2 FY27 figure is $820m (+13.4% on Q2 FY26's $722.8m). A Q1 beat of about $13m flowed through would hold or nudge the range to the street; a new Q2 guide midpoint below about $810m would read as a cut.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY26 guide cut: -17.75%. Q3 FY26 FY raise: +4.81%. Q4 FY26 initial FY27 guide about at street: +6.81%.
findings.why_not_priced: Guide direction is the swing factor, and options price a 10.1% move for it. The sourced point is that the guide was built with stated conservatism, so the street is not asking for much above it. If the market feared another cut, the skew would be steeper than +2 vol points.
findings.independence: Conservatism factors in the August guide: https://www.blocksandfiles.com/hci/2026/08/27/nutanix-grows-despite-hardware-price-rises/5292962 . Q2 street from Benzinga, undated: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NTNX/earnings-forecasts

findings.finding: The Earnings Whispers whisper is $0.71 EPS against $0.60 published ('nearly 20% above'), and its preview says traders expect last quarter's profit upside ($0.60 against $0.49) to repeat. So the buy-side EPS bar sits above consensus, though the published EPS consensus itself is disputed ($0.53-0.60).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26's 22% EPS beat paid +6.81%. Q1 FY26 matched EPS but missed revenue: -17.75%. Revenue and guide drive this stock more than EPS.
findings.why_not_priced: A whisper is an expectation, not a fact. It is filed because it says the real EPS bar is above the printed one. The bar is disputed, so this is capped small.
findings.independence: Benzinga's $0.53 consensus, as surfaced in search: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/NTNX/earnings-forecasts

findings.finding: Spot $55.39 sits below the lowest of 17 analyst targets ($63; mean $79.27). Targets were not cut through the 24% fall, and Rosenblatt kept $75 on 2026-11-17. The sell side has not capitulated: a clean print leaves room for re-rating calls, while a miss would bring target cuts.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Nov 2025 miss, several target cuts followed (Goldman $95 to $75, Morgan Stanley $90 to $82).
findings.why_not_priced: Targets lag price. The gap is a two-sided sensitivity, not a direction, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: The board added $750m to the buyback authorization at Q3 FY26 (2026-05-27). With the stock down about 24% during and after Q1, the Q1 release may show heavy repurchases or a further authorization.
findings.why_not_priced: Q1 repurchase volume is not disclosed until the release. It is an inference about use and is sized small.

findings.finding: The same fiscal quarter a year ago (Q1 FY26, reported 2025-11-25) missed revenue ($670.6m against $676.6m consensus) because late-quarter bookings carried start dates outside the quarter. Q2 was guided $705-715m against $748.8m street and FY cut to $2.82-2.86bn, and the stock fell 17.75%. October quarter-end is where the future-start-date risk has shown up before.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: -17.75% on that print. The next three prints beat and went +3.98, +4.81, +6.81.
findings.why_not_priced: It is history, so it is priced in the 14.4% straddle. It is filed because the FY27 guide now explicitly assumes more future start dates, which shrinks this risk, though not to zero.

findings.finding: Net revenue retention fell from 109% to 106% (per the EW preview), and FY27 FCF margin is guided to about 28% against 29% in FY26 as more customers pay annually or use third-party financing. Both point to slower expansion within the installed base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: NRR is not isolated in past reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Already reported, so largely priced. A further NRR step-down in Q1 would be new, but no evidence shows one either way.

findings.finding: AMD bought 4,136,789 Class A shares at $36.26 (about $150m) in May 2026 as part of an AI alliance. This is equity financing that funds a partnership, not distress.
findings.why_not_priced: Six months old and fully public. It buys a partnership and has no bearing on the Q1 number.

baseline_tension: The skew (+2.03, mild downside paid) leans slightly against the long lean. The 20-day run-up of -23.85%, about 10 points worse than software, supports it, because the bar has fallen into a print whose last three reactions were positive. The negatives found (Q1 seasonal slippage history, Maner's exit, supply macro) are what the skew prices, so p_up stays only slightly above 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 5 (macro proxy inside the guide) and lesson 6 (lands inside what the company guided): DRAM/TrendForce finding cut from -0.5 to -0.2.
Lesson 5 (inference, not a company number) and lesson 1 (the market already looked through it): Maner departure cut from -1.0 to -0.7.
Lesson 6 (disputed EPS bar, capped small): whisper-EPS finding cut from -0.5 to -0.3.
Lesson 5 (proxy sized small): Lenovo counterparty cut from +0.5 to +0.4.

Left standing: the beat-pattern (+1.0) and price-path (+1.0) findings. The revenue bar is sourced to a company guide plus two agreeing estimates, and this name has paid for top-of-guide beats three times. Lesson 7: the skew is mild (+2.03) and short interest is not crowded, so the long lean is not cut further. abs_move_pct and p_up are unchanged.
